source_refs.note: FeatureDiscoveryArtifact FDA-CTX-20260915-01-global-option, producer portal-explorer, same run

observations: 12/12 provided network capture files read and mapped to ACT-ID. No capture is missing for any ACT-ID referenced in portal-evidence.json's scenarios/actions this run — no BLOCKED needed on that basis.

Global Option CRUD uses TWO different mechanisms depending on operation: CREATE/CLONE/DELETE are REST (POST /api/global-options, POST /api/global-options/{id}/clone, DELETE /api/global-options/{id}); EDIT is a client-constructed Hasura GraphQL table-level mutation (updateGlobalOption -> update_global_options_by_pk) hitting POST /api/graphql, NOT a REST PUT/PATCH. Confirmed directly from request bodies/operationName+query text in ACT-01-01-001..004, not inferred.

The artwork<->Global Option link is confirmed at the API layer: artwork layer object in the POST /api/artworks response (ACT-06-01-001) contains customization_type='global_option' and global_option=862 (the id created in ACT-01-02-001). This same layer sub-object is echoed again, unchanged, inside the POST /api/campaign-artworks response (ACT-06-02-001), independently re-confirming the link at the campaign-attach step.
assumptions: api_context.environment/base_url taken from the literal URLs seen in every captured entry (https://staging-api.teeinblue.com) plus bootstrap-request's stated staging environment; not independently re-verified by api-explorer beyond what portal-explorer already confirmed (OBS-target-verify).
unknowns: Whether the Global Option 'Category' field (global_option_category_id) has any relation to the type-specific category pickers ('Select additional options category' / 'Select one vector category') seen on Additional Option and Vector Category types, and whether those in turn are the SAME underlying table as the /additional-options and /vectors (asset-category) objects. See documented_observed_mismatches and payload notes below — treated as INFERRED at best, not confirmed.

Whether 'required: true' observed on the artwork layer using 'Use an existing global option' (ACT-06-01-001) is a default of that personalization_type or is copied from the referenced Global Option's own 'required' field (which was data.required=false on Global Option 862's own create payload, ACT-01-02-001) — the two values (layer required=true vs option data.required=false) do NOT match, which is itself worth flagging as an open question, not concluded either way.

Full request_body shape for 4/7 create-type samples (ACT-01-04-001, 01-05-001, 01-06-001, 01-07-001) was not captured in the network files provided — only response_body was available for those. Field-presence claims on the REQUEST side are therefore based on only 3/7 samples (001, 002, 003).

Response-body field completeness varies across the 7 create samples (created_at/updated_at/data/global_option_category_id missing in some captures) — cannot distinguish genuine field-absence from capture truncation without re-capture; not treated as a schema fact.

conflicts.topic: Global Option 'Category' field default value: bootstrap-request statement vs this run's API/DOM observation

side_a.statement: Field 'Category' trên Global Option instance mặc định 'Uncategorized'.

side_b.source: this run: raw/network/ACT-01-01-001.json through ACT-01-07-001.json (global_option_category_id: null in every captured create response) + portal-evidence OBS-005 (create-form Category picker shows literal 'No category', zero records) + OBS-001 (list page's per-row Category combobox shows 'Uncategorized' as a display-only fallback, not tied to any global_option_category_id value)
side_b.statement: No API response this run ever returned a non-null global_option_category_id, and no 'Uncategorized' category record exists — 'Uncategorized' only appears as list-UI display text when global_option_category_id is null, it is not a real category id/name coming from any API payload.

conflicts.resolution: NOT RESOLVED by api-explorer — handed to orchestrator/reviewer per contract §8. Both statements kept.

documented_observed_mismatches.documented: bootstrap-request (input/bootstrap-request.json, object_target.note) states the field 'Category' on a Global Option instance defaults to 'Uncategorized'.
documented_observed_mismatches.observed: Every captured create/edit/clone response this run shows global_option_category_id=null (never a non-null value tied to any 'Uncategorized' record); the create form's Category picker itself displays literal 'No category' with zero selectable options (portal-evidence OBS-005). 'Uncategorized' only appears as list-page display-only fallback text (OBS-001) when global_option_category_id is null — it does not correspond to any category id/name returned by any API call this run.
documented_observed_mismatches.resolution: NOT resolved by api-explorer — both statements kept in conflicts[], handed to orchestrator/reviewer.

security_surfaces.surface: Client-constructed Hasura GraphQL table-level mutation 'updateGlobalOption' (update_global_options_by_pk) called directly from the browser to POST /api/graphql, with the _set object (data/name/global_option_category_id/updated_at) fully assembled client-side.
security_surfaces.risk_note: Structurally the same pattern already flagged for asset-category's insert_cliparts (FEAT-03 area). No cross-tenant sample or forged pk_columns.id was attempted this run — cannot conclude whether Hasura permission rules restrict which rows the mutation can target, or whether tenant scoping is enforced server-side vs relying on the client-supplied x-acting-user-id header. Observation only, not a safe/unsafe conclusion.

security_surfaces.surface: Client-constructed Hasura GraphQL list/aggregate query 'getData' (global_options_aggregate + global_options(offset,limit,where,order_by)) called directly to POST /api/graphql.
security_surfaces.risk_note: Client controls where/order_by/offset/limit — typical shape of direct Hasura exposure to the browser. Not tested for cross-tenant data leakage (e.g., manipulating 'where' to read another store's rows) this run.

security_surfaces.surface: Tenant/user scoping via client-supplied request header 'x-acting-user-id' (observed value 266, matching Linh explorer's user_id) present on every REST and GraphQL request this run, rather than solely a server-derived value from the session cookie.
security_surfaces.risk_note: Not tested whether the server validates this header against the authenticated session's actual tenant, or trusts it as-is (no forged-header / cross-tenant fixture sample captured this run). Flagged as an open question only, consistent with the same open question already noted for asset-category.
